Day 7 of teaching you how to create with AI.

The secret to cinematic AI videos isn't just the prompt. It's what happens BEFORE you generate your first shot. 🎬👀

Someone asked me yesterday how to create a good storyboard, so let's talk about it!

Whether you're creating a fashion film, product advert, UGC video, or AI movie, here's your simple roadmap. 👇

1️⃣ Start with the idea. Know what you want to create and the story you want to tell.

2️⃣ Structure your story. Give it a beginning, middle, and ending.

3️⃣ Break it into shots. Decide what happens in every scene and what your audience should see.

4️⃣ Direct the camera. Choose your angles, close-ups, camera movements, and transitions.

5️⃣ Upload your references to ChatGPT. Include your model, character, or product images and ask it to create a shot-by-shot storyboard.

6️⃣ Review before generating. Check the flow, character consistency, outfit details, and camera directions.

7️⃣ Bring it to life. Use your storyboard in Google Flow, generate your shots, and edit them together in CapCut.

Remember, a storyboard isn't just a collection of beautiful images. It's your visual roadmap!

Plan the story before you generate the scenes. That's how you gain more control over your AI videos. 🔥

Did xAI just kill every voice AI startup, again?

Grok Voice 3.0. Their most intelligent speech-to-speech model yet. And the benchmarks are brutal.

86.9 on the Speech-to-Speech Index. GPT-Live-1: 83.2. Gemini 3.8 Live: 82.6. The highest score ever recorded.

98.5% on speech reasoning. Highest of any model tested.

97.0% on conversational dynamics. 94.8% on task completion. First on both.

1070 Elo on human preference. GPT-Live-1 sits at 1048.

Time to first audio: under a second, at 40% lower latency than the frontier models it beats.

It is not a demo. At SpaceX it resolves 70% of Starlink support calls on its own.

Starlink takes 20,000 support calls a day across languages. Millions more voice conversations run inside Tesla cars, every day.

Pricing: $0.08 per minute of audio. $0.025 per completed task, the lowest in the comparison.

Live today in the API and the Voice Agent Builder. Existing agents were switched over automatically.

1/  This one is somewhat older paper (DL lifecycle wise) but I think this is an important regularization idea to combat reward hacking! I’ve personally done this (before even reading this paper) and it’s stabilizes the loss landscape. 

DDRL: keep training on data while doing RL. They combine reward maximization with the usual diffusion loss on real/synthetic samples. That denoising loss helps keep generations realistic as the model learns to get higher rewards.

https://t.co/2PKj6zkGhd

RL post-training rewards final answers, but which steps deserve credit?

An AR LM has one left-to-right path to a given answer. A diffusion LM can reach it through many denoising paths, yet most RL methods give every step the same score, even those that hurt.

So why not simply credit each step by how much it changes the expected reward?
